name: the-box
title: The Box: how a steel container remade world trade
summary: A one-minute history of the shipping container.
sources: Further reading: Marc Levinson, The Box (Princeton University Press, 2006)

beats.say: Almost everything you own came to you inside a steel box.

shot.title: The Box
shot.subtitle: How a steel container remade world trade

say: Before the box, cargo was loaded by hand.
Sack by sack. Crate by crate.

beats.say: It was slow. It was heavy. And it was expensive.

say.text: Then a trucking man named Malcom McLean asked a simple question.
say.speak: Then a trucking man named Malcolm Mc Clane asked a simple question.

say: Why not lift the whole trailer onto the ship?

events.label: The Ideal X sails from Newark to Houston
The world agrees on standard sizes

say.text: In April 1956 his ship, the Ideal X, left Newark for Houston.
say.speak: In April nineteen fifty six, his ship, the Ideal Ex, left Newark for Houston.

say: Ten years later, containers were crossing the Atlantic.

say.text: And by 1968, the world had agreed on standard sizes.
say.speak: And by nineteen sixty eight, the world had agreed on standard sizes.
It carried just fifty eight containers.

say.text: Loading a ship by hand cost $5.86 a ton.
say.speak: Loading a ship by hand cost five dollars eighty six a ton.

beats.say: Ports were rebuilt around the box.
And shipping became so cheap that where a thing is made stopped mattering very much.
